text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eight people are charged with the theft of 96 million shillings ($1.7 million) from the Standard Chartered Bank in February.
- The police will vet all participants in Tuesday's Langata constituency by-election to pre-empt any violence.
- Up to 5,500 Kenyan students have been defrauded of about 20 million shillings in a scam involving a London professional exams body and a Nairobi business college.
- The National Executive Council of opposition party FORD-Kenya denies saying it would support the ruling Kenya African National Union party's candidate for the Langata by-election.
- The managing director of Kenya Cooperative Creameries says the milk and butter shortages now hitting Kenyans are due to reduced production.
- United States Ambassador to Kenya Prudence Bushnell says the U.S. is deliberating on the need for continued investment to Africa.
- The government launches the National Women's Development Programme and Fund.
- Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru currently on an official visit to Sweden could be extradited from the country for unbecoming behaviour.
- Hungry pupils desert school in the drought-hit area of Kitui in eastern Kenya.
